# Regex


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

``` apl
]help •r
```

`•r pattern` compiles a Rust regex. It returns a keyed vector of
functions that share the pattern: `match`, `position`, `length`,
`groups` and `replace`. Positions count characters from 0.

`template p.replace text` expands `$0`, `$1`, `${name}` and `$$` in
`template`. Flags go in the pattern, as in `(?i)`.

Errors: DOMAIN for invalid patterns, including look-around and
backreferences, and for non-text arguments; SYNTAX for wrong valence;
LIMIT for oversized results.

Patterns use [Rust regex
syntax](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/#syntax). Here `p` finds runs
of digits:

``` apl
p←•r "[0-9]+"
p.match "abc123def45"
p.position "abc123def45"
p.length "abc123def45"
'#' p.replace "abc123def45"
```

    "123" "45"

    3ₓ 9ₓ

    3ₓ 2ₓ

    abc#def#

Search returns a vector, including zero or one match. Matches don’t
overlap. Lengths count characters:

``` apl
p←•r "é|🐈+"
p.position "aé🐈🐈z"
p.length "aé🐈🐈z"
p.match "abc"
```

    1ₓ 2ₓ

    1ₓ 2ₓ

    0⍴⊂""

`groups` returns the captured strings of each match, without the whole
match. An unmatched optional capture gives `""`:

``` apl
p←•r "([a-z]+)([0-9]+)"
p.groups "ab12 cd3"
```

    [["ab" "12"] ["cd" "3"]]

In a replacement, `$0` is the whole match and `$$` is a literal `$`. An
unknown or unmatched capture expands to `""`:

``` apl
p←•r "(?P<word>[a-z]+)([0-9]+)"
"${word}:$2:$$" p.replace "ab12"
```

    ab:12:$

`(?i)` ignores case, `(?m)` makes `^` and `$` match at line breaks, and
`(?s)` lets `.` match newlines. Use Each to search several strings:

``` apl
p←•r "(?i)cat"
≢⍤p.match¨"Cat cat" "dog"
```

    2ₓ 0ₓ

Empty matches occur at character boundaries:

``` apl
p←•r ""
p.position "é🐈"
'-' p.replace "é🐈"
```

    0ₓ 1ₓ 2ₓ

    -é-🐈-

`lib/regex.apl` supplies `pattern (f regex_replace) text`. It applies
`f` to each matched string and keeps the text between matches:

``` apl
•load "lib/regex.apl"
"[0-9]+" ({⍕2×•json ⍵} regex_replace) "a12 b3"
```

    a24 b6
